title: ESQL: Fix equals hashCode for functions

timeline.author: Alexander Spies

timeline.message:
Fix UnaryScalarFunction's equals+hashCode

They are strictly worse than the corresponding methods inherited from
EsqlScalarFunction.
timeline.author: Alexander Spies

timeline.message:
Do not assert different hash codes

Collisions must be considered okay.
timeline.author: Alexander Spies
Alexander Spies

timeline.message:
Remove Log::equals and hashCode

The inherited methods from Function are equivalent or better (e.g.
hashCode takes class name into account).

timeline.message: Use correct config for ser/de in csv tests
timeline.author: Alexander Spies
Alexander Spies

timeline.body:
Fix https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/104393.

For any descendants of `EsqlConfigurationFunction`, the `hashCode` and `equals` methods did not take the actual configuration into account. It is important that they do, since functions like `NOW` provide different results depending on the configuration; in particular, the actual `now` datetime is contained in the `EsqlConfiguration`.

Also, clean redundant implementations of `hashCode` and `equals` in other functions, whenever the inherited methods could just be used.
I went over all inheritors of `EsqlScalarFunction` for this.

timeline.body: Hi @alex-spies, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
The implementation in `Function` also hashes the class name, likely causing fewer collisions.
Redundant, the implementation in `Function` already checks equality based on the children (all of the expressions).

The config was _always_ important for serialization and subsequent deserialization to produce equal results; now our csv tests actually catch this: without using the correct `EsqlConfiguration`, differences are being detected in e.g. `date_format` (and rightly so).

@not-napoleon maybe we should (separately to this PR) add test cases for functions that rely on the `EsqlConfig`. E.g. `NOW` actually derives its value from the config, which maybe could use a nice randomized test.

reply.body: That's a good point.  Let's get a ticket open for that, so we don't forget.  for `NOW` at least, it might make sense for it to not use `AbstractFunctionTestCase` at all, since it doesn't really have any parameters we need to randomize, null, type check, etc.
